name: munlockall
description: munlockall() unlocks all pages mapped into the address space of the calling process, allowing them to be swapped out by the kernel if necessary. This reverses the effect of mlockall(), which locks memory into RAM.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, errno is set

errors.description: The caller is not privileged (requires CAP_IPC_LOCK) to perform the operation, especially on older kernels like Linux 2.6.8 and earlier.
Locking or unlocking would exceed memory limits or some specified address range does not correspond to mapped pages.

bugs: In Linux 4.8 and earlier, bugs in accounting locked memory could cause failures in related calls; in Linux 2.4 series, mlockall() flags were incorrectly inherited across fork, and privileged processes dropping capabilities after mlockall() could lead to allocation failures.
